title: FinTwin: a point-in-time system-dynamics digital twin for corporate liquidity stress testing
description:
FinTwin turns a company's SEC XBRL filings into a calibrated stock-and-flow (system-dynamics) model of its finances and stress-tests it with Monte Carlo simulation. Every parameter is estimated from point-in-time filings, so backtests are free of look-ahead and restatement bias.

This archive contains the Python reference engine, the point-in-time XBRL pipeline, the research experiments and statistics, the scripts that generate every table, figure and number in the accompanying paper, the TypeScript browser engine and dashboard, and data snapshots.

Main results (paper in docs/paper): frozen before COVID-19, the twin ranks 2020-21 cash burn of 333 S&P 500 non-financial companies better than the Altman, Ohlson and Zmijewski scores, but a trailing free-cash-flow margin ranks it better still, and neither the twin nor the classic distress scores rank the shock-induced part of the burn. Fed the revenue that actually followed, the twin identifies where a margin pass-through rule misjudges cash flow (incremental correlation 0.30 across 2,661 firm-years, positive in every year 2014-2023), and its revenue forecasts beat a seasonal random walk and exponential smoothing.

Interactive version: https://spiliosdimakopoulos.github.io/fintwin/
